Article Title: 'Wanted to tarnish image': Delhi Police on man held over alleged AI poster showing cop sexually assaulting woman
Article Text:
Police said Nadeem admitted during questioning that he used AI tools to create such videos. (PTI)

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Tuesday said 24-year-old Nadeem Ahmed , arrested for allegedly creating and circulating an AI-generated fake poster falsely depicting a police officer sexually assaulting a woman during a protest, made it “to tarnish the image of the police and turn protesters against them. ”Addressing a press conference, additional deputy commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Manjeet said Nadeem admitted during questioning that he used AI tools to create such videos.Police said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and had been running an Instagram account since April. The account had around 24,000 followers and 1,226 posts, according to investigators.“On 3rd October, we saw a footage circulating on social media wherein it is being shown as the CCTV footage from the protest site. It is being portrayed that an individual in Police uniform is misbehaving with a woman. Through social media, the identity of the officer is being revealed. When we examined it, we found that one Nadeem Ahmed, a r/o Palwal, Haryana was running that channel. We arrested him. In the initial questioning, he told us that he is an independent journalist. He told us that he had studied till class 10 in Madrasa of Saket, Delhi,” police said.“He also told us that he is a 10th-fail. Upon further questioning, he told us that he has AI tools, with the help of which he keeps making such videos. When we asked him why he made such videos, he told us that he wanted to tarnish the image of Police so that the protesters coming there would start harbouring hatred for the Police and start attacking them. We took immediate cognisance of this and arrested him. We will take him into police remand and further question him. His source of funding and accomplices are matters of investigation. We have seized his phone for further analysis. He became more active during CJP protest. So, we will analyse if this is part of any bigger conspiracy...” police added.Nadeem, who studied at a madrassa in Saket and failed to clear Class 10, was arrested on Monday and produced before a court, which granted police custody for further investigation.Police are also investigating whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy and are working to identify them. His phone has been seized for forensic and further analysis.The arrest comes amid a controversy over an assistant commissioner of police accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.ACP Vivek Bhagat was promoted to the rank of additional deputy commissioner on Monday along with three other officers from his batch. However, the order assigning him additional charge was withdrawn on Tuesday.According to the government, Bhagat requested "of his own volition" not to take charge until a full inquiry into the alleged harassment of women journalists is conducted and "satisfactorily concluded".Earlier, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had accused Delhi Police of refusing to register an FIR against an additional DCP over an alleged assault on an independent journalist and demanded action against the officer. Separately, complaints by three women journalists alleging harassment by police personnel had triggered protests and demands for action.
Article Summary: Police said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and had been running an Instagram account since April. The account had around 24,000 followers and 1,226 posts, according to investigators. Police are also investigating whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy and are working to identify them.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke claims CJP activists receiving police notices threatening October 10 protest 'could turn violent'
Article Text:
‘One nation, one political party’: Abhijeet Dipke targets Centre, alleges pressure on CJP activists

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday targeted the centre and alleged that “One Nation, One Election” was merely a slogan and alleged that the government’s intention was to establish “one nation, one political party”.He also claimed that activists of the Cockroach Janta Party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests."I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heartbreaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, telling them not to participate in the agitation at Jantar Mantar. They also asked about the source of the expenses for travelling to Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.Dipke questioned how police could predict that the agitation would turn violent. He also questioned the police directive to CJP activists against making social media posts that could allegedly lead to violence."We speak about (Mahatma) Gandhi and B R Ambedkar. Do they think it is violent?" he asked.The CJP had earlier welcomed the INDIA bloc’s proposed protest on Tuesday, saying its own October 10 mobilisation should be seen as a broader call by the youth rather than an event led by any particular organisation.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said everyone, including political parties, student organisations, activists and members of the public, should assert their rights through peaceful protests.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said the organisation welcomed the INDIA bloc’s planned protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday.“We welcome all peaceful protests. Everyone should make efforts, be it INDIA bloc or other student organisations or activists, or common people. Everyone needs to assert their rights,” Das told a press conference.Das said repeated protests indicated that people were not being heard. “If people are hitting the streets repeatedly then there is a problem,” he said, adding that taking to the streets was the “last resort” for people who felt their concerns were not being addressed.At the press conference, Das also claimed that the CJP had received information from “well-wishers” within the establishment that its leaders could be arrested ahead of the October 10 protest. “Well wishers have informed us that meetings are taking place and there is a high possibility that CJP leaders could be arrested,” he claimed. “It does not matter if we are arrested or detained because this fight is about the young generation.“Even if we are arrested or detained the protest will go on because this is the fight for our future,” he asserted. “Fear of FIR, fear of jail has evaporated -- it won't work anymore.”Das said Jantar Mantar had become a “symbol of hope and victory” and asserted that protesters would sit wherever police stopped them. “Wherever police stops us, we will sit there and that will become Jantar Mantar,” he said.Das also referred to the Supreme Court’s Monday remarks on the controversy surrounding Form 6, accusing the Election Commission of misrepresenting the court’s position. “The EC sought to clarify in its press statement that the Supreme Court upheld changes in Form 6. Today, the Supreme Court has said the EC lied,” he said.Chief Justice Surya Kant, during a hearing on Monday, said the Supreme Court had not approved any modification to Form 6. The clarification assumes significance as the EC, in its September 26 statement following a meeting of the full commission, had said the “declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court”.On the CJP’s October 10 mobilisation, Das said the protest should be viewed as a broader youth movement rather than the initiative of a particular organisation. “You should not consider the call for protests on October 10 as our call or someone else's call. This is the call by the youth and Gen Z. We are one part of that.”His remarks came against the backdrop of an online exchange over the weekend between the CJP and sections aligned with the Congress, after a social media post compared CJP national convener Abhijeet Dipke with AISA president Neha Bora. Dipke and Bora rejected any suggestion of rivalry, while CJP leaders accused sections of the “liberal ecosystem” of attempting to undermine Dipke.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj also weighed in, cautioning against replacing one form of “hero worship” with another.The exchange brought differences between the CJP and sections of the Congress into the open. Some Congress leaders have been wary of the CJP’s emergence, given the AAP background of several of its prominent faces, while the AAP has backed its recent mobilisations.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleges that ‘One Nation, One Election’ was merely a slogan. He also claimed that activists of the Cockroach Janta Party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests. CJP co- convener Saurav Das said everyone, including political parties, student organisations, activists and members of the public, should assert their rights through peaceful protests.

Article Title: ‘Unacceptable’: India reacts after Russian strike injures Indian sailor on Black Sea ship
Article Text:
India has strongly condemned the attack on the MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea, which tragically resulted in the deaths of two foreign nationals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India on Monday condemned the attack on a civilian commercial vessel in the Black Sea as “completely unacceptable” after a Russian drone strike reportedly killed two foreign nationals and injured crew members, including an Indian sailor.The vessel, MV ROYAD MAMMADOV, was attacked outside Romania's territorial waters, according to reports. Three Indian nationals were among the crew, with the Indian Embassy in Romania confirming that all three were safe and receiving medical care.One of the three Indians was injured in the attack and was being treated at Constanța County Hospital. Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke with the three crew members and the hospital's chief physician, who confirmed that they were in good health and receiving necessary care.“All three Indian nationals are safe. We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy said.External affairs minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the United Nations General Assembly, condemned attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers across major maritime routes.“New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations. This is completely unacceptable,” Jaishankar said.The Indian mission said it was in contact with relevant authorities to establish further details of the attack and ensure the welfare of the Indian crew members.
Article Summary: Russian drone strike reportedly killed two foreign nationals and injured crew members, including an Indian sailor. Three Indian nationals were among the crew, with the Indian Embassy in Romania confirming that all three were safe and receiving medical care. One of the three Indians was injured in the attack and was being treated at Constanța County Hospital.

Article Title: Delhi court grants bail to 17 students, journalists arrested during CEC protest
Article Text:
Delhi Police accused of misconduct with female journalist at Jantar Mantar..

Court sets bail conditions for accused

Police seek custody, defence cites right to protest

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday night granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists arrested during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, and directed jail authorities to ensure medical treatment for those who sustained injuries.In four separate orders passed between 9 pm and 9:25 pm, Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Animesh Kumar of Patiala House Court ordered the release of all 17 accused in connection with an FIR registered at Parliament Street police station.The court directed that the accused be released on furnishing a personal bond with one surety of the like amount. It also said they should be released immediately if their custody was not required in any other case.The court specifically directed the jail superintendent to ensure necessary medical treatment for accused who had sustained injuries, as advised by the medical officer.The accused have been directed not to directly or indirectly induce, threaten or influence anyone acquainted with the facts of the case or tamper with evidence. They have also been restrained from committing any offence while on bail.They must provide their correct permanent and residential addresses and active mobile numbers, keep the numbers operational and inform the court of any change in address.They are also required to appear before the concerned court on every date of hearing and cannot leave the country without prior permission.The court said the investigating agency would be free to seek cancellation of bail if any of the conditions were violated.The FIR was registered under Sections 223(a), 221, 132, 190, 191(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act.Police alleged that the accused were part of an unlawful assembly, obstructed or blocked public space, manhandled police personnel and damaged public property.The investigating officer had sought 14 days of judicial custody, arguing that the accused could commit further offences or interfere with the investigation.The defence opposed the plea, arguing that the accused were young and that several were students exercising their democratic right to dissent and protest. Defence counsel also submitted that no individual role had been specified against the accused in the grounds of arrest.The defence pointed out that while police claimed around 50 people were protesting, only 17 had been arrested. It also argued that no CCTV footage of the alleged incident had been produced before the court.The defence further submitted that some of the accused had sustained injuries and their medical examinations had not been conducted immediately after the incident.The court observed that the allegations were serious and noted that a police official had allegedly sustained injuries. However, it said the right to protest peacefully could not be disputed, while assaulting police officials on duty was a serious concern.The court also noted that, except for the offence under Section 132 of the BNS, the offences invoked were bailable in nature. It further observed that the accused did not appear to be habitual offenders and had their entire careers ahead of them.Considering the facts and circumstances, the court ordered their release on bail subject to the specified conditions.The court directed that the accused be produced before the concerned court on October 6 and ordered that a copy of the bail order be supplied to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, for information and necessary compliance.
Article Summary: A Delhi court on Monday night granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists arrested during a protest. The court directed jail authorities to ensure medical treatment for those who sustained injuries. The accused have been directed not to directly or indirectly induce, threaten or influence anyone acquainted with the facts of the case or tamper with evidence.

Article Title: US nuke test detection experiment bid to assert its hegemony: Ex-nuclear chief
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Former chief of Atomic Energy Commission of India, Anil Kakodkar, who played a key role in the Pokhran nuclear weapons tests, said the main aim of the US conducting what is called a non-proliferation experiment last week was to assert its global nuclear hegemony and prevent other nations from conducting atomic tests.On Sept 30, the US conducted an experiment which will enable it to detect whether countries are carrying out low-yield nuclear explosions.Kakodkar told TOI, “The US is attempting to get more sensitivity in terms of nuclear tests detection. There is a generic understanding that nuclear tests will not be carried out. But what if a country executes a test camouflaged?”Asked whether the motive of the test jeopardised nuclear sovereignty of countries, he said the main aim was to assert global US nuclear leadership and stop other countries from carrying out atomic weapons tests.A recent study by Federation of American Scientists says that currently India has 190 nuclear warheads and has enough military plutonium for 140 to 225 nuclear warheads.Anil Anand, considered the father of India’s nuclear submarine programme, quoted US National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) and told TOI that in the experiment researchers gathered measurements using a broad suite of advanced sensors, including accelerometers, seismometers, chemical and radiotracer samplers.He said, “Together these measurements will improve scientists’ understanding of the signatures produced by underground explosions and strengthen US’ ability to detect and characterise nuclear explosive events. ”According to NNSA, it “conducted a subsurface, non-nuclear chemical high-explosive experiment” at the Nevada National Security Site. An FB post by NNSA states, “If foreign countries test in secret, we will know.The goal? Keeping the US one step ahead.” It further said the experiment assumes significance in the context of China supposedly having conducted a nuclear test in June 2020 secretly.“It takes nuclear expertise to detect nuclear activities, and experiments like these ensure America remains unmatched in detection,” said Brandon Williams, NNSA administrator. “Trump Administration has made it clear that the US will lead from a position of strength. You cannot evade American innovation. With this experiment, we are sending a clear message that under this administration, America will never be outmatched. ”
Article Summary: Former chief of Atomic Energy Commission of India, Anil Kakodkar, said the main aim of the US conducting what is called a non-proliferation experiment was to assert its global nuclear hegemony. On Sept 30, the US conducted an experiment which will enable it to detect whether countries are carrying out low-yield nuclear explosions.

Article Title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
Article Text:
The idea of an informal meeting with SC judges on simultaneous polls was first mooted by DMK MP and senior advocate P Wilson

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court had initially fixed a schedule for an "informal interaction" with members of the Parliament committee examining the bill for simultaneous elections, the panel's chairperson, P P Chaudhary, told reporters Monday, stating that the SC later found it "not appropriate" and called it off, apparently after some opposition MPs criticised the proposed meeting.He, however, defended the proposal, saying there were precedents of parliamentary committees interacting with SC judges because of their expertise and knowledge of constitutional matters.Sources said the idea to meet SC judges was first mooted by DMK MP P Wilson, a senior advocate, and was informally deliberated within the committee before it took this up with the SC.The meeting was fixed for October 6 but the SC secretary general last week informed the committee of the cancellation."They (senior SC judges) are of the opinion that as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review before the Supreme Court, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. The proposed meeting is accordingly cancelled," the secretary general said.Chaudhary said an email was sent to the Parliament secretariat by SC officials on September 22, stating that a meeting had been fixed on October 6 at 4.30 pm and the law ministry also sent the relevant material to the court."After about eight or nine days, some issues were raised publicly. Later, SC cancelled the meeting. If SC felt it was not appropriate, there was no need to pursue the matter. There was no need to create or give further publicity to the issue. "Sources said, on September 18, the Lok Sabha secretariat first wrote to the SC secretary general, conveying the committee's desire to undertake a "local study visit" for "informal discussions" with the CJI and other judges on simultaneous elections.Wilson, through a seven-page letter to the committee, defended the proposal and said in the spirit of broad-based consultation, he had suggested that the panel hear the views of the CJI and other judges. "Unfortunately, due to political objections surrounding this meeting, it was decided to call off the meeting because of unnecessary and unfortunate circumstances caused by vested interests," he said. Opposition MPs, including senior advocate Kapil Sibal, had slammed the proposed meeting.
Article Summary: Supreme Court had initially fixed a schedule for an "informal interaction" with members of Parliament committee examining the bill for simultaneous elections. The meeting was fixed for October 6 but the SC secretary general last week informed the committee of the cancellation. Opposition MPs, including senior advocate Kapil Sibal, had slammed the proposed meeting.

Article Title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
Article Text:
23-year legal duel (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Nearly 23 years after it stayed the arrests of some journalists following the Tamil Nadu assembly passing a breach of privilege resolution against them, the hearing scheduled before a seven-judge Supreme Court bench Wednesday, which promised to be a legal duel over the media's right to free speech versus the ambit of legislative privilege, appears to be an exercise for the records.For TN assembly, senior advocate Raju Ramachandran, flanked by attorney general R Venkataramani and solicitor general Tushar Mehta, told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the cause of action for the writ petition did not survive and the issue had become academic as the assembly withdrew the resolution imposing 15-day sentence on some journalists in 2004.A bench of CJI Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V Mohana is scheduled to take up the petitions filed by N Ravi and S Selvam, then editors of 'The Hindu' and 'Murasoli' newspapers, respectively.Following the Nov 7, 2003, assembly resolution, arrest warrants were issued against the two editors and some journalists.CJI Kant said a seven-judge bench would assemble Tuesday, take the 2004 resolution on record and dispose of the petitions. Pendency in SC has increased to over 90,000 cases.
Article Summary: Hearing scheduled before a seven-judge Supreme Court bench Wednesday. It promised to be a legal duel over the media's right to free speech versus the ambit of legislative privilege. TN assembly told a bench of CJI Surya Kant that the cause of action for the writ petition did not survive.

Article Title: Rawat seeks meet with Congress brass as Kumari Selja slams his yatra plan
Article Text:
File photo: Ex-Uttarakhand CM Harish Rawat

NEW DELHI: With return of rumblings in Uttarakhand Congress on the eve of assembly elections, former CM Harish Rawat has sought time with party brass to clarify his "thanksgiving yatra" in the wake of AICC's strong censure.A terse letter by Kumari Selja, AICC in-charge of state, has dubbed Rawat's yatra as a "parallel programme" that is not in Congress' interest. She has said the party must put up a "united front" ahead of the polls. Crucially, she also underlined to Rawat that his yatra has neither been approved by her nor by the state president, and he has made some controversial statements recently.Sources said Rawat, while going ahead with his yatra, has responded to the letter and urged an appointment. They said a discussion may be held between Rawat and Selja this week, possibly Wednesday or Thursday, after the demonstration against the EC in Dehradun.Rawat's sudden embarking on a yatra has stumped the party as the notoriously factionalised state unit has managed to put a united front in recent months. The party brass have been undertaking solo public outreach and holding joint programmes amid strong optimism that Congress is well placed to oust the ruling BJP from power in the hill state.In the current leadership structure, Rawat has been forced to cede ground to younger leaders.Perturbed, party sources told TOI that AICC censure made it clear to Rawat that his yatra has not gone unnoticed. While the party does not want to force the issue, it is learnt to have been inundated with complaints."The party is firm that Rawat will have to follow the discipline and toe the official campaign programme," a senior manager said.
Article Summary: Ex-Uttarakhand CM Harish Rawat seeks time with party brass to clarify his "thanksgiving yatra" AICC in-charge of state has dubbed Rawat's yatra as a "parallel programme" that is not in Congress' interest.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: High court quashes PSA detention of Shopian man for ‘showing anti-national tendencies’
Article Text:
J&K high court

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir high court quashed the preventive detention of a man booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of showing a disposition towards anti-national activities, terming the allegations against him “prima facie vague”.The detention of Mashooq Ahmad Shah of Shahlatoo was in violation of constitutional guarantees envisaged under Article 22(5) of the Constitution, Justice Rajnesh Oswal said in his order Saturday, directing his immediate release if he was not wanted in any other case.The Shopian district magistrate on Dec 23, 2025, ordered the detention of Shah based on a police dossier that cited intelligence reports and said that he had “shown a tendency towards anti-national activities in his locality and other parts of the district ... and hatred against the state and govt in order to radicalise and instigate the youth towards anti-national activities”.The dossier further mentioned that Shah “remains a perpetual concern for the security agencies” and “could potentially be used as a conduit by terrorist outfits to build underground networks”. His conduct indicated “he has no respect for judicial proceedings and the law of the land”, it added.Shah was lodged in Jammu’s Kot Bhalwal jail. He moved the HC, arguing that the grounds of detention were false, incorrect, vague and non-existent. The allegations “are illusory and without any material basis”, he said.Justice Oswal concurred with the petitioner that the charges against him were vague and “bereft of necessary particulars”. The court said the state failed to identify the persons and associations with extremist leanings with which it alleged Shah maintained contact, nor did it specify who the youths were with whom the petitioner attempted to establish contact and when.
Article Summary: Mashooq Ahmad Shah of Shahlatoo was booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of showing a disposition towards anti-national activities. Shah was lodged in Jammu’s Kot Bhalwal jail. He moved the HC, arguing that the grounds of detention were false, incorrect, vague and non-existent.

Article Title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
Article Text:
Russian drone strike hits Turkish cargo ship in Black Sea, killing 2 (representative image)

Three Indians among crew, all reported safe

Zelenskyy says captain killed in drone attack

Vessel was headed from Ukraine to Italy

NEW DELHI: At least two people were killed and several crew members, including an Indian national, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire aboard a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea.The Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel, identified as MV Royad Mammadov, and that one of them was injured and receiving medical attention.“We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties (foreign nationals) while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy said it was in close contact with the relevant authorities to establish further details about the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals.Indian ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke to the three Indian crew members who were receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. The embassy said the hospital's chief physician confirmed that all three were in good health and receiving necessary care.“Amb @manojifs spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. He also spoke with the hospital’s Chief Physician, who confirmed that all three are in good health and receiving necessary care. The ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support,” the mission said.It later said that all three Indian nationals were safe.“We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy added.The nationalities of the two people killed in the incident were not immediately known.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that two Russian drones had struck a civilian vessel carrying corn in neutral waters.“A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye,” Zelenskyy said.He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard the vessel and that the ship's captain had been killed. The fate of another person was still being established, he said.“Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board. As of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship’s captain was killed. My condolences. The fate of one other person is still being established,” Zelenskyy said.He added that 11 crew members had been rescued, including one who was injured.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly proposed concrete measures to de-escalate the conflict and improve security in the Black Sea.“Pressure is needed to restore global food security. And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help,” he posted.Romania's interior ministry said its Coast Guard was alerted about the fire at around 11 am local time after the vessel was reported in the country's exclusive economic zone, about 30 nautical miles (55 km) south of Sfantul Gheorghe in Tulcea County.The ministry did not confirm what caused the fire. Romanian media reported that the vessel had been hit by a drone southeast of a Black Sea oil platform, but the reports had not been immediately verified by authorities.Romania's Naval Authority identified the vessel as the Royad Mammadov. According to MarineTraffic, it is a general cargo ship flagged to Saint Kitts and Nevis. It had departed Ukraine's port of Izmail and was headed for Italy.Romanian authorities said 11 crew members had been rescued and two deceased people had been found. Injured crew members were airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment.The Black Sea has faced heightened security concerns amid the Russia-Ukraine war, with attacks affecting commercial shipping and port infrastructure.The incident came a day after a 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in a Russian strike in Ukraine's Sumy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and stepped up efforts in recent months to help resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging with both Kyiv and Moscow.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has “good ideas” to find a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.
Article Summary: Russian drone strike hits Turkish cargo ship in Black Sea, killing 2. Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel. Injured crew members airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment. Incident came a day after 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in Russian strike.

Article Title: ‘Compassion in judging is not favour or leniency’: Supreme Court Justice Vikram Nath
Article Text:
Justice Nath said the courts must ensure that legal principles do not overshadow the human realities.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath on Monday said compassion in judging should not be mistaken for favour or leniency, but should instead mean understanding the human circumstances behind a legal dispute without compromising fairness or the law.Speaking at the second Prof. (Dr) N R Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture, Justice Nath said the courts must ensure that legal principles do not overshadow the human realities of those involved in a case.The annual lecture was held on the theme "Judging with Compassion: Human Understanding in the Practice of Law"."Let me say what compassion in judging is not. It is not favour and it is not leniency. It is not deciding for a party merely because that party is weak, or allowing emotion to overcome evidence. And it is certainly not abandoning the law. Compassion in adjudication means understanding before judging -- the discipline of seeing the human circumstances in which a legal controversy arose. Its opposite is not strictness, which is sometimes exactly what an institution needs. The opposite of compassion is indifference," Justice Nath said as per news agency PTI.Justice Nath, who is also the executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority, stressed that being impartial does not mean becoming detached from the human consequences of judicial decisions."The blindfold on Lady Justice does not mean she cannot see. It means she does not look at who stands before her before deciding what is right. She still weighs and weighs with care. A judge must be impartial, but never indifferent," he said.He said the justice system must also consider how its procedures are experienced by people who come before the courts, particularly those who may already be vulnerable."For the survivor made to relive her trauma in the witness box or the litigant who cannot follow the language of the proceedings, the process is what justice actually feels like," he said. "We must ask whether, for too many, it has itself become a trauma," he said.Referring specifically to cases involving survivors of sexual violence and child witnesses, Justice Nath said courts could adopt a trauma-informed approach without compromising judicial standards."a trauma-informed courtroom is not a softer courtroom," he said.He also warned against allowing public sentiment to influence judicial fairness, particularly at a time when cases can be tried in the media before courts have reached a conclusion."A compassionate court is not a court with a favourite side. It is a court that can understand every side, without becoming captive to any. In an age of trial by television, when the public often decides before we do, that takes the courage to be fair to the person everyone has condemned and the courage to be firm with the person everyone has forgiven," he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath said compassion in judging should not be mistaken for favour or leniency. He said the courts must ensure that legal principles do not overshadow the human realities of those involved in a case. The annual lecture was held on the theme "Judging with Compassion: Human Understanding in the Practice of Law"

Article Title: Accountability will be fixed if people's grievances remain unresolved: UP CM Yogi Adityanath

Article Title: ‘Police can’t remain mute spectators’: Delhi HC dismisses pleas for fresh probe into 2019 Jamia violence
Article Text:
Delhi HC rejects SIT probe pleas in Jamia violence case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Delhi high court on Monday dismissed petitions seeking an independent probe into alleged police brutalities against students during the December 2019 violence at Jamia Millia Islamia. The court observed that police cannot be expected to remain “mute spectator” when a gathering turns violent.A bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said the police did not enter the university premises at the outset when the assembly was peaceful, but intervened after the situation outside the campus escalated and the crowd moved into the university.“The police intervention, therefore, has to be viewed in the prevailing law and order situation which had developed at that time,” the court said.‘Police cannot be expected to remain inactive’The bench said the right to peaceful protest was not in dispute. Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution protect freedom of speech and expression and the right to assemble peacefully without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions.These rights do not, however, extend to causing any violence or destruction of property, it said.“Once a gathering ceases to remain peaceful and the circumstances disclose violence, commission of cognisable offences or a threat to life or property, the police cannot be expected to remain inactive or as mute spectator merely because the gathering is taking place within a university campus,” the court observed.The petitions sought an independent judicial inquiry into the violence, an investigation into alleged police excesses and compensation for injured students.“The events of December 2019 undoubtedly generated considerable public concern and gave rise to serious allegations regarding the conduct of various stakeholders,” the court said.The bench noted that protests on December 15, 2019, had escalated into violence around the university, including stone-pelting, burning of buses and other vehicles, damage to public property and attacks on police personnel.The high court also noted shortcomings in the police response, referring to the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) inquiry, which found that the use of tear gas shells inside the university library could have been avoided.It said a university was a place of learning and academic activity, and this “crucial aspect” must be considered while exercising police powers.“That consideration cannot, however, be taken to mean that the police are prohibited from entering a university campus in all circumstances,” the court said.It added that university authorities should, wherever circumstances permit, be informed and consulted before police intervention. However, an immediate threat to life or property or a rapidly developing law-and-order situation may leave no time for prior communication or permission.The court noted that criminal cases had been registered, an investigation conducted by the Delhi Police Crime Branch's Special Investigation Team (SIT), and charge sheets filed before competent courts. The NHRC had submitted its report in May 2020.“No subsequent incident or material has been brought to our notice to show that the violations of guidelines as alleged in these petitions have continued or have been repeated,” it said.
Article Summary: Delhi high court dismisses petitions seeking an independent probe into alleged police brutalities against students at Jamia Millia Islamia. Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said the police did not enter the university premises at the outset when the assembly was peaceful.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Monday issued a “fact check” amid the controversy over reported changes to Form 6, calling Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s claim that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had “changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally” misleading.In its response, the EC said the order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, issued on June 24, 2025, had received the unanimous approval of the Commission and was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in its judgment dated May 27, 2026.The poll panel also cited its Press Note No. 120 dated September 26, 2026, pointing to point 1(iii), which states: “The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.”The EC's response came after Rahul alleged in a post on X that the CEC had changed Form 6 “illegally and unilaterally”, citing the recent Supreme Court observation.EC officials also clarified that Form 6 itself had not been changed, but that a declaration had been attached to the form under the Bihar SIR order, as quoted by PTI.The clarification came after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modification to Form 6 used by the EC during the SIR exercise in various states.“Any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When records are produced, we would like to see who has modified it,” a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said.Form 6 is the application used by eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral roll.The declaration was attached to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR, which began with the EC's June 24, 2025 order. The declaration sought additional details, including information about the applicant's parents.According to EC officials, the form itself remained unchanged, while the declaration was a separate document attached to it for the SIR exercise. Outside SIR, the forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply.The declaration was later withdrawn from the EC's online portals.The online version of Form 6 and the declaration also used a single OTP for both, rather than requiring separate OTP verification, which had led to suggestions that the declaration was part of Form 6.The EC also rejected claims that it had withdrawn its September 26 press note and shared the document to show that it remained available.
Article Summary: The Election Commission issued a “fact check” amid the controversy over reported changes to Form 6. Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi claimed that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had “changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally” The EC said the order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, issued on June 24, 2025, had received the unanimous approval of the Commission.

Article Title: 'Fighting this battle in our own way': AAP to skip opposition march to EC office over SIR row
Article Text:
AAP MP Sanjay Singh (File photo)

NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Monday said it would not participate in the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission office, saying it was "fighting this battle in our own way. "Senior AAP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh said protests against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were being held daily at different places across the country.He added that the AAP was not even using its own banner, as it considers the issue a "people's movement" concerning citizens across the country and believes everyone should participate in it."The CJP's (Cockroach Janta Party) protest is also being held, and different organisations are also holding protests. The Left is also protesting in different places. As far as tomorrow's protest is concerned, it is the INDIA bloc's protest. So, the AAP is not part of it. We are fighting this battle in our own way," Singh told reporters at the Parliament House complex.Two parties formerly aligned with the INDIA bloc, the AAP and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), had also skipped the alliance's September 30 meeting to decide its response to an Indian Express report concerning the EC.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav was absent as well, but sent party representatives to attend the meeting.Some other leaders, including Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Jharkhand chief minister and Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) president Hemant Soren, participated virtually.After the meeting, attended by the Congress and 18 other opposition parties, INDIA bloc leaders announced that they and all its MPs would march to the Election Commission's headquarters in the capital on October 6. The leaders would also meet President Droupadi Murmu to raise concerns over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls.The call for the protest came amid a controversy over the functioning of the EC, with opposition parties alleging irregularities in the poll panel's handling of the SIR exercise.An investigation by The Indian Express last month reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR, which they alleged had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation. Sandhu and Joshi also reportedly termed specific changes made to voter enrolment forms "unauthorised" and "illegal".The EC has rejected suggestions of a split within the three-member panel, maintaining that decisions relating to the SIR were taken unanimously.
Article Summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) said it would not participate in the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission office. AAP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh said protests against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were being held daily.

Article Title: Two Saudi airports in Jazan and Najran targeted as tensions with Yemen's Houthis escalates
Article Text:
The attacks came after the Houthis claimed to have launched a fresh wave of missile and drone strikes. (Photo: X/MarioNawfal)

Saudi airports assess damage

Houthis claim strikes on airports, Aramco facility

Airports in Saudi Arabia 's Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, injuring three people and causing limited damage, according to the kingdom's aviation authority, as tensions with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels escalated.The attacks came as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces stepped up a major offensive to retake territory from the Houthis along the Red Sea coast. Saudi Arabia has intensified airstrikes in support of the campaign.The Houthis have responded with missile and drone attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia, including airports, oil facilities and military sites.Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said it was assessing the damage at King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz International Airport and Najran International Airport, Reuters reported.The authority said measures were being taken to ensure the safety of passengers and staff and protect the kingdom's civil aviation system. The attacks came after the Houthis claimed to have launched a fresh wave of missile and drone strikes targeting key Saudi facilities.The Houthis said their operations targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, Abha International Airport and a military base in Khamis Mushait, Reuters reported.The claimed strikes mark an escalation in the Saudi-Houthi confrontation, with the conflict increasingly spilling beyond Yemen's borders and threatening Saudi economic and military infrastructure.The escalation followed territorial gains by Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces along Yemen's western coast, including areas near the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait.Yemeni government forces advanced towards Mocha after recapturing areas near the strait, putting further pressure on the Houthis.The intensifying conflict has also triggered the activation of the Mecca defence pact, with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye moving to implement their collective-defence commitments.
Article Summary: Airports in Saudi Arabia's Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, injuring three people and causing limited damage. The attacks came as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces stepped up a major offensive to retake territory from the Houthis along the Red Sea coast.

Article Title: Hyderabad tea stall owner walks into police station, sets himself ablaze
Article Text:
P Sudhakar, a tea stall owner in Bhimgal, attempted suicide by self-immolation at the local police station (Visuals credit: X)





HYDERABAD: A man attempted suicide by setting himself ablaze on the Bhimgal police station premises on Monday morning, prompting police personnel and complainants present at the station to douse the flames and shift him to Nizamabad Government Hospital.The man, P Sudhakar, a resident of Bhimgal, runs a tea stall at the old bus stand in the town.According to police, Sudhakar was booked in a petty case for running his shop during late-night hours. Police said the case was registered as part of their routine enforcement duties.Nizamabad police commissioner P Sai Chaitanya said there was no direct connection between police and the reason that led Sudhakar to attempt suicide.“There is no fault on the part of police in the incident that occurred at the Bhimgal police station,” the commissioner said.According to the preliminary information received by police, a grocery shop located opposite Sudhakar’s tea stall was allegedly unhappy that he was not buying cigarettes from the shop.The shop owner allegedly sent two men to threaten Sudhakar, police said.The commissioner said Sudhakar had apparently been upset over the alleged threats by the men and subsequently came to the police station carrying a bottle of petrol and a matchbox.Around 9:45 am, he allegedly attempted suicide on the station premises.Police personnel and complainants at the station immediately intervened, doused the flames and shifted Sudhakar to the government hospital for treatment.His condition was reported to be serious.Police said the incident was being examined based on the preliminary information available and maintained that the police case against Sudhakar was unrelated to the alleged threats by the men.
Article Summary: P Sudhakar, a tea stall owner in Bhimgal, attempted suicide by self-immolation at the local police station. Police personnel and complainants at the station immediately intervened, doused the flames and shifted him to the government hospital. His condition was reported to be serious.

Article Title: 'Revenge for Gaza': What flydubai Omani co-pilot told interrogators after failed attack

‘Revenge for Gaza’: Flydubai co-pilot’s chilling account of alleged Israel plot

Israel’s security agency Shin Bet has sent interrogators to the United Arab Emirates to participate in the questioning of Hamam al-Hammami, the flydubai copilot accused of attempting to carry out a " terror attack " aboard a flydubai flight last week, as reported by The Times of Israel .According to two Israeli officials familiar with the probe, al-Hammami told UAE interrogators that he had planned to crash the flight into Ben Gurion Airport even before he was hired by Dubai-owned flydubai.Channel 12 also reported, citing two Israeli officials, that al-Hammami said he was acting “in revenge for Gaza” and wanted to “die as a martyr”.A source briefed on the UAE investigation said al-Hammami had previously operated a flight to Tel Aviv earlier this year and had considered hijacking and crashing that aircraft but ultimately did not do so.Channel 12 further reported, citing two sources, that a Mossad official told Israeli Cabinet ministers on Sunday that al-Hammami had made brief visits in recent years to several countries hostile to Israel. The two Israeli officials said al-Hammami told interrogators that he applied to fly for flydubai after searching for airlines operating flights to Tel Aviv.A third source said Israel was being kept continuously updated by the UAE on the investigation.Disaster aboard the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight was averted after passengers and crew subdued co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, who allegedly attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar with an emergency crash axe while the aircraft was over Jordan. The UAE prosecutor general has described the incident as a “terrorist attack”.According to a timeline reported by Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera, al-Hammami had requested a prayer break shortly before attacking Machchhar. Despite being wounded, the captain managed to open the cockpit door, alerting an off-duty pilot travelling in the passenger cabin. Passengers then rushed into the cockpit and helped subdue al-Hammami.After his initial plan was disrupted, al-Hammami allegedly attempted to crash the aircraft into the desert by forcing it into a steep descent and trying to damage the controls. Off-duty pilots took over the aircraft and issued an emergency alert before the plane was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where it landed at 10.57 am. Article Title: Trump signs order to ease diesel costs, ‘save millions of dollars’ for farmers
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

Diesel still costs well above last year

Trump drops diesel export ban

US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) signed an executive order aimed to ease the burden of high diesel prices on farmers, truckers and other businesses, as fuel costs continue to put pressure on Republicans ahead of the November midterm elections.Trump announced the move during a campaign stop in Grand Island, Nebraska, saying that loosening limits on the tax-free use of red-dyed diesel would save farmers “millions” and help bring down the cost of goods and groceries.“Pete and Jim, this should absolutely ensure your election, I guarantee you that,” Trump said, addressing Republican governor Pete Ricketts and governor Jim Pillen.The order directs states to increase the availability of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is used in farming, construction and other industries. It also calls on states to consider waiving certain fuel taxes and includes so-called non-enforcement of dyed diesel limitations.Red-dyed diesel is exempt from federal and state excise taxes. The administration says that temporarily easing restrictions would reduce costs for businesses that depend on diesel.“The typical trucker will save more than $100 every time they fill up,” Trump said as he signed the order before a crowd in Grand Island.“Farmers will also save millions and millions of dollars, and this order will also drive down the cost of all goods and to go to grocery prices very substantially.”The steps also include the treasury department reviewing certain taxes on diesel.Ten states accounting for roughly a third of US diesel sales had already taken steps to allow wider use of dyed diesel by Friday, according to research firm ClearView Energy Partners, cited by Politico. Several states had also waived taxes on diesel used in agricultural vehicles.The move comes as diesel prices remain sharply higher than a year ago.The average price of diesel fell to $6.32 a gallon on Monday, down 13 cents from the previous week but still $2.63 higher than a year ago, according to AAA.Fuel prices have surged amid the ongoing war against Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The conflicts have contributed to a significant decline in the amount of diesel available on the global market.Exports of American diesel have also risen to record levels since the US and Israel launched a war with Iran in February and Ukraine began targeting Russian refineries.The red-dyed diesel measure follows weeks of uncertainty over how the administration would respond to rising fuel prices.Trump had repeatedly backed an outright ban on diesel exports as agriculture-state Republicans, including Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley, pushed for action to lower costs for farmers.Energy secretary Chris Wright and White House energy advisers had been working on alternatives.But on Friday, Trump ruled out a diesel export ban and said he had never really considered one, after Europe agreed to release fuel from its diesel reserves.Agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins said Monday morning that Trump would announce additional short-term relief for farmers in Nebraska and that she would also discuss the issue during a stop in Iowa.High fuel and grocery prices have become a major concern for rural voters, many of whom have backed Trump and Republicans in recent elections. Nebraska farmers and ranchers have also been angered by the administration's plan to allow more imports of foreign beef.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order aimed to ease the burden of high diesel prices on farmers, truckers and other businesses. The order directs states to increase the availability of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is used in farming, construction and other industries. It also calls on states to consider waiving certain fuel taxes.

Article Title: Karnataka OKs auto approval of period leave for govt staff
Article Text:
Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar

App-authorised leave can’t be reversed





BENGALURU: Women govt employees across Karnataka will no longer need to justify their need for menstrual leave with their sanctioning authority, as the state govt Monday ordered automatic approval of all such leave applications through the Kartyavya app.In a move aimed at ensuring menstrual leave remains an entitlement rather than a matter of discretion, the latest directive from the Praja Seva department has made the leave-sanctioning process virtually automatic, eliminating the need for human intervention. Officials have been instructed to ensure that employees apply for menstrual leave only through the Kartyavya app.The Kartyavya app is an AI-powered mobile attendance registration platform. Once a menstrual leave application is authorised through the app, no sanctioning authority can withhold, question or reverse the decision.The decision follows recent reports that women employees were facing hurdles in availing the leave, with applications allegedly being held up and some sanctioning officers even questioning the need for such leave.The state govt has now made it clear that such discretion cannot be exercised once the prescribed conditions are met. The circular issued by Praja Seva department said state govt had already extended a day’s menstrual leave every month to women govt employees. The benefit was specifically introduced to do away with the need for a medical certificate.“An application that fulfils the prescribed conditions should be sanctioned promptly, and the sanctioning authority has no discretion to reject it,” the circular further clarified.
Article Summary: Women govt employees across Karnataka will no longer need to justify their need for menstrual leave with their sanctioning authority. The state govt Monday ordered automatic approval of all such leave applications through the Kartyavya app. The decision follows recent reports that women employees were facing hurdles in availing the leave.

Article Title: Lucknow floods: 60 boats deployed, more on way, UP govt steps up relief
Article Text:
District administration has intensified flood relief operations as Gomti River levels rise in Lucknow





LUCKNOW: The district administration has intensified flood relief operations in low-lying areas as rising Gomti River levels continue to inundate several localities, prompting deployment of additional boats, distribution of relief kits and tighter security in affected neighbourhoods.District magistrate Vishakh G said nine gram panchayats in Bakshi Ka Talab tehsil remain waterlogged. Within the Lucknow Municipal Corporation limits, Faizullaganj and nearby settlements such as Mama Colony, Lauramau and Daud Nagar are among the worst hit, with water entering residential lanes and disrupting movement.Relief kits supplied by the Uttar Pradesh relief commissioner’s office are being distributed to affected families. Officials said each kit contains 10 kg wheat flour, 10 kg rice, 10 kg potatoes, along with chana, pulses, bottled drinking water and other essential items.To maintain connectivity and speed up relief delivery, the administration has deployed 60 boats in Faizullaganj. Vishakh G said more than 20 motorised boats from Ayodhya and other districts are expected to arrive by Tuesday, which is likely to expand evacuation capability and allow residents to commute for basic needs.Security has been stepped up in submerged localities, with SDRF boats assisting local police in patrolling flooded stretches and monitoring locked homes. The district magistrate said one person was recently arrested for allegedly attempting to steal from abandoned houses in an inundated area.Calling the situation challenging, Vishakh G appealed for public cooperation and urged residents to follow official advisories.Meanwhile, executive engineer Mukesh Kumar Vaish of the irrigation department’s Gomti river division reported that the water level at Gau Ghat was 108.45 metres on Monday evening, while the Central Water Commission’s Hanuman Setu gauge recorded 107 metres and the Gomti Barrage level was about 106.75 metres.Vaish said differences in readings occur due to the river’s natural gradient, with slopes of around 10–15 cm per km leading to variations between gauge points. At Hanuman Setu, the danger mark is 109.5 metres and the highest flood level is 110.85 metres, according to the CWC.
Article Summary: District administration has intensified flood relief operations as Gomti River levels rise in Lucknow. Nine gram panchayats in Bakshi Ka Talab tehsil remain waterlogged. More than 20 motorised boats from Ayodhya and other districts are expected to arrive by Tuesday.

Article Title: ‘Learn Hindi or leave job’: Bengaluru Zomato warehouse manager booked for threatening Kannada-speaking staff

A shift manager named Ashok Muttayy was accused of telling Kannada-speaking workers to learn Hindi





BENGALURU: A 31-year-old shift manager at a Zomato-rented warehouse near Nelamangala was booked for allegedly telling Kannada-speaking workers to learn Hindi or leave their jobs.Ashok Muttayy, who hails from Andhra Pradesh, worked as a shift manager at the warehouse in Madanayakanahalli.According to police, a video surfaced on social media showing Ashok speaking to workers in Hindi during an official interaction. When a worker asked him to speak in Kannada, Ashok allegedly refused and told the workers to learn Hindi or leave their jobs.Soon after, a group of pro-Kannada activists gathered outside the warehouse and demanded action against Ashok.“We registered a suo motu case and filed a petition against Ashok for his act. Ashok later apologised for his conduct,” an investigating officer told TOI.
Article Summary: Ashok Muttayy, 31, was booked for allegedly telling Kannada-speaking workers to learn Hindi or leave their jobs. A video surfaced on social media showing Ashok speaking to workers in Hindi during an official interaction. Pro-Kannada activists gathered outside the warehouse and demanded action against Ashok.

Article Title: CJP assault case: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets regular bail after 3-week interim relief
Article Text:
Bhardwaj had earlier been granted three weeks' interim bail with strict conditions.

Why was Bhardwaj arrested?

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Tuesday granted regular bail to social media influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj in connection with the alleged assault on the father of a student activist during a protest at Jantar Mantar.Bhardwaj had earlier been granted three weeks' interim bail with strict conditions. The court has now granted him regular bail after considering his conduct during the interim bail period.A detailed order, including the bail conditions, is expected to be passed later in the day, according to news agency ANI.On September 15, the court had granted Bhardwaj three weeks' interim bail and said his conduct during the period would be considered before deciding his regular bail plea.It had barred him from posting, publishing or discussing the case, his defence or the complainant's family on social media or any media platform.He was also restrained from contacting the complainant, his daughter or any witness and from tampering with evidence.The court had observed that “bail is an expression of the court’s trust, and it is not a trophy to be displayed”, while cautioning against public celebrations following release on bail.Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr on September 4, hours after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protested outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.The action followed outrage over an interview in which Bhardwaj claimed that he had “cracked the skull” of the student activist's father during the June 23 protest and that he escaped arrest because of his 'political connections'.Police, however, had disputed the severity of the injuries claimed by Bhardwaj, saying the man suffered a simple head injury during a scuffle.Bhardwaj was subsequently remanded to judicial custody on September 7 and lodged in Tihar Jail. He was released from the prison on September 18 after being granted interim bail.
Article Summary: Bhardwaj had earlier been granted three weeks' interim bail with strict conditions. The court has now granted him regular bail after considering his conduct during the interim bail period. A detailed order, including the bail conditions, is expected to be passed later in the day.

Article Title: Pilot who 'never planned to fly': Mumbaikar Smit Machchhar's journey from textile course to saving 180 lives on flydubai flight
Article Text:
Captain Smit Machchhar managed to regain control of a flydubai aircraft after a co-pilot attacked him

From textile engineering to cockpit

From SpiceJet to flydubai

The flight that plunged thousands of feet





MUMBAI: Captain Smit Machchhar never grew up dreaming of flying planes. In fact, when he was 19, his career path appeared to be taking him in an entirely different direction — towards his family's textile business.An aviation seminar during a management course changed that.More than a decade later, the Mumbaikar found himself at the controls of a flydubai Boeing 737 MAX during one of the most terrifying moments of his flying career — after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit as the aircraft was carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Despite being injured, Machchhar is reported to have fought back and helped prevent the aircraft from plunging further. The plane had dropped thousands of feet in a matter of seconds before passengers and crew intervened and the aircraft was eventually diverted to Saudi Arabia.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later identified Machchhar as the captain and praised his actions, saying he had helped prevent a major disaster.Machchhar's journey into aviation was anything but conventional.In a podcast interview recorded around a year before the incident, he recalled that becoming a pilot was not a childhood ambition.After school, he initially enrolled in a textile engineering course because he expected to eventually contribute to his family's business.He later opted for a management course to prepare himself for the business.It was during that course, when he was just 19, that he attended an aviation seminar."Unlike a lot of other aviators right now, aviation was not like a childhood dream," Machchhar said in the interview.The seminar changed his plans.His decision to enter aviation initially worried his mother."My mom was scared," he recalled, explaining that commercial aviation was far less familiar to people around him 15-17 years ago. His father, however, was more comfortable with his decision.Machchhar subsequently completed his commercial pilot training in New Zealand before obtaining his Boeing 737 type rating at the Flight Safety Training Centre (FSTC) in Manesar, Gurgaon.Machchhar joined SpiceJet in 2011 and spent more than a decade with the airline, eventually becoming a senior commander and Line Training Captain.According to his professional profile, he accumulated more than 9,500 flying hours with SpiceJet, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command. As a Line Training Captain, he was responsible for training, assessing and mentoring other pilots while ensuring adherence to operational and safety procedures.He moved to flydubai in June 2022 as a direct-entry captain and has since been flying the Boeing 737 fleet.His profile lists more than 9,750 hours of flying experience and experience on the Boeing 737-800 and Boeing 737 MAX 8/9.A senior pilot who had trained Machchhar previously described him as a "very decent and sober person" who was always willing to learn.Machchhar's brother is also a pilot with flydubai.The flydubai flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 166 Israeli citizens, when the incident unfolded.According to flight-tracking data, the Boeing 737 MAX descended from roughly 30,875 feet to 16,750 feet in just 29 seconds. Flightradar24 recorded an extreme descent rate of around 30,000 feet per minute.Reports said the Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a knife. The captain was injured but managed to resist while the aircraft was in danger of losing control.Passengers and crew eventually entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.The aircraft was then diverted and landed at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Two additional pilots who had been travelling as passengers were also on board and later took over the aircraft.The severity of the descent surprised aviation experts. Former United Airlines pilot and aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said he was surprised the aircraft remained intact after the extreme manoeuvre, while aviation investigator Jeff Guzzetti said the aircraft had enough altitude left for the pilots to recover.The aircraft also reportedly suffered damage to its rudder during the descent.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar managed to regain control of a flydubai aircraft after a co-pilot attacked him. The plane had dropped thousands of feet in a matter of seconds before passengers and crew intervened and the aircraft was eventually diverted to Saudi Arabia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later identified the captain and praised his actions.

Article Title: Why ‘kaun se wale papa’ remark led to man’s conviction
Article Text:
The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC (AI Image)

“Dekho papa aa gaye, don’t cry.”

“Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark, “Kaun se wale papa?”, made when she told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Though the two had no prior dispute, the court held that the remark implied the woman had multiple partners and questioned the child’s paternity.Judicial magistrate first class Moksha Bains, in a Sept 24 judgment, said the remark was not an innocuous inquiry about the child’s father but carried an insinuation about the woman’s sexual propriety and fidelity. “The expression, when addressed to a woman in the aforesaid setting, is not an innocuous inquiry as to the identity of a person,” the judge observed, adding that its “obvious insinuation” was that there could be more than one man who could be described as the child’s father.The case dates back to March 23, 2021, when Priyanka Gupta was walking with her three-year-old daughter near RBI Enclave Gate in Paschim Vihar. As the child cried, Gupta told her,Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected,Gupta initially ignored the remark and, about two minutes later, handed over the child to her husband after he arrived in a car.She later informed her father-in-law, who called the police, following which an FIR was registered at Paschim Vihar East police station under Section 509 IPC.In his statement under Section 313 CrPC, Lal admitted making the remark but claimed it was not made with any “ill intention”. He also alleged false implication, with the defence arguing that Gupta wanted him removed from the street corner where he had run his ironing business for seven years.Rejecting the defence, the court observed: “The explanation offered by the accused that the words were spoken without ‘ill intention’ is a bare assertion. No surrounding circumstance has been brought on record from which the remark could reasonably acquire an innocent meaning.”The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, as the insult must have the requisite nexus with her modesty. In this case, however, it held that the remark was personally directed at Gupta and made immediately after she referred to her child’s father, carrying a sexually derogatory insinuation concerning her relationship with men and the child’s paternity.The court held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted Lal under Section 509 IPC.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark. Priyanka Gupta told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected, “Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”

Article Title: Hyderabad woman Sandhya Reddy becomes mayor of Sydney council
Article Text:
Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney





HYDERABAD: A Hyderabad-origin woman, Sandhya Reddy, was elected mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney, Australia, on Tuesday. According to members of the migrant community, she is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia.Affectionately known as Sandy, Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014 and was elected to the Strathfield Council as an independent councillor in 2021. In 2023, she was elected deputy mayor of the council.A lawyer by profession, Reddy was born and raised in Hyderabad, where she also pursued her education before moving to Australia in 2005. She has been living in the country ever since.Members of the Indian community in Australia hailed her achievement, describing it as both "symbolic and significant" for the country's multicultural communities.
Article Summary: Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney. She is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia. Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014.

Article Title: Jaipur man held for killing pregnant live-in partner, burying body in rented house courtyard
Article Text:
The murder came to light on Sept 27, (Representative Image)





JAIPUR: Police here Tuesday arrested a 20-year-old man for allegedly strangling his pregnant live-in partner and burying her body in the courtyard of their rented house in Prestige Garden Colony, Bindayaka.DCP (West) Prashant Kiran identified the accused as Pravesh Kumar alias Haggu. Police said he allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners.The murder came to light on Sept 27 when the house owner found Kiran’s body buried in the courtyard. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.During questioning, Kumar told police that he strangled Kiran with one hand and covered her nose and mouth with a cloth with the other. He initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that Kiran had died by suicide and that he buried her body after panicking, police said.Kumar and Kiran had come to Jaipur from their village about two months ago. Kiran was pregnant and Kumar was living with her and taking care of her.The two used the same mobile phone. Kumar worked odd jobs to support them, police said.After the murder, Kumar allegedly switched off the phone and went to Samod on foot to visit the Hanuman temple.Police said he told them he went there to “wash away his sins”. He returned to work and stayed there from Sept 24 to 26.On Sept 27, after suspecting that the murder had been discovered, Kumar allegedly collected Rs 500 in wages from the factory owner and fled Jaipur.Police teams began searching for him after recovering Kiran’s body. Investigators examined CCTV footage, analysed technical evidence and prepared a route chart to track his movements.A police team eventually detained him on Agra-Lucknow Expressway and arrested him after questioning.Kumar is a resident of Parsa Auliya Lalpur village under Safdarganj police station in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Pravesh Kumar allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.

Article Title: Blast at MRPL refinery sends loud boom across Mangaluru, thick smoke billows
Article Text:
A loud explosion-like sound was reported from the Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd premises on Wednesday.
