MANGALURU: A blast followed by a fire was reported at the CHT unit, the Hydro Sulphur Treatment Unit of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL), on Wednesday.The fire has since been brought under control, city police commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy CH said.One person, identified as Rajesh Baptist, sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. He is undergoing treatment in the ICU and doctors said he is out of danger.Six other people who suffered minor injuries at an adjacent office were given outpatient treatment and underwent medical check-ups, police said.The city police commissioner, deputy commissioner and Zilla Panchayat CEO are present at the site. Police said there was no major cause for concern and that necessary precautionary measures were being taken.MRPL also confirmed that there were no casualties in the incident and appealed to people not to panic.The blast sent a loud boom across several kilometres, with thick black smoke billowing from the refinery premises. Residents of Jokatte and Surathkal reported that their houses shook and doors and windows vibrated following the explosion.The blast was also reportedly heard at Mangaluru airport, where windows of the administrative office rattled. Fire tenders and emergency teams were rushed to the refinery, while ambulances were seen leaving the premises.On the advice of the district administration, Mangaluru airport is conducting a visual inspection of vital installations in and around the airport, including the Precision Approach Lighting Category I systems and peripheral roads, to check their operational readiness.Dakshina Kannada MP Capt Brijesh Chowta said he was in constant touch with MRPL officials, the police commissioner and Fire and Emergency Services Department officials and was proceeding to the spot to assess the situation.He appealed to people to remain calm, refrain from spreading rumours or misinformation, and cooperate with the administration. Local hospitals were also instructed to remain prepared as a precautionary measure.
Article Summary: A blast followed by a fire was reported at the Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) on Wednesday. One person sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. Residents of Jokatte and Surathkal reported that their houses shook and doors and windows vibrated.

Article Title: In 1934, America created a $1 conservation stamp for duck hunters; it has since helped protect more than 6 million acres of wetlands
Article Text:
The Duck Stamp. Image Credit: BirdNote

How the 1934 $1 Duck Stamp began protecting wetlands

Image Credit: Ducks.org

The hunting requirement became a conservation tool

How Duck Stamp money reaches wildlife habitat

What makes the stamp useful beyond hunting

The artwork has become part of the programme

In 1934, the United States introduced a small annual stamp that linked waterfowl hunting directly to wetland conservation. The Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act, signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on 16 March that year, required waterfowl hunters aged 16 and over to buy a stamp. The first one cost $1 and featured mallards, with artwork created by conservationist and cartoonist J.N. Ding Darling. More than nine decades later, the Federal Duck Stamp has raised over $1.3 billion and helped conserve more than 6 million acres of habitat, according to the US Fish & Wildlife Service (US FWS).The idea emerged during a difficult period for both people and wildlife. BirdNote reported that the early 1930s were marked by the Great Depression, drought and widespread damage to wetlands. Waterfowl populations had already been weakened by hunting pressure and the loss of breeding habitat as wetlands were drained.The Federal Register provides the legal history of the programme. Congress passed the Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act on 16 March 1934, and Roosevelt signed it the same day.The law required waterfowl hunters aged 16 or older to purchase a stamp every year. The money was intended to provide a dedicated source of funding for protecting habitat.The first stamp was designed by Jay N. Ding Darling, who was then director of the Bureau of Biological Survey, the predecessor of the US Fish & Wildlife Service. The US FWS says Darling's design began an annual tradition in which wildlife art became part of a conservation funding system.The unusual feature of the programme was its direct connection between hunting and habitat protection. Hunters were the main group required to purchase the stamp, turning an annual hunting requirement into a source of money for wetlands.According to the Federal Register, the programme had generated more than $1 billion by 2018 and supported conservation of more than 6 million acres of waterfowl habitat. The agency also noted that the protected areas benefit many species beyond waterfowl, while wetlands can help with flood control and water purification.The US FWS now reports that more than $1.3 billion has been raised since 1934. Its Federal Duck Stamp programme states that 98 cents of every dollar spent goes towards acquiring vital habitat or conservation easements within the National Wildlife Refuge System.The funds do not simply support the production of the stamp. They are deposited into the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund, which is used to purchase or lease wetlands and other wildlife habitat.The US FWS explains that more than 6 million acres have been acquired using Federal Duck Stamp revenue. More than 300 national wildlife refuges have been created or expanded with the help of these funds, while at least one refuge in nearly every state has benefited.The programme also supports smaller wetlands and surrounding uplands through Waterfowl Production Areas. These sites can provide important breeding and nesting habitat, while conservation easements can protect land without necessarily ending private ownership or its working-land uses.The stamp's value extends beyond the people who are legally required to buy it. The US FWS says anyone can purchase a Federal Duck Stamp, including conservationists, birdwatchers and collectors. A current signed stamp can also provide free admission to national wildlife refuges that charge an entrance fee.The wetlands protected through the programme have practical benefits as well. According to the US FWS, they can help purify water, control floods and reduce soil erosion and sedimentation. They also create opportunities for outdoor recreation.The National Wildlife Federation reported in 2026 that more than 98 percent of Duck Stamp proceeds go directly towards acquiring and protecting wetland habitat for the National Wildlife Refuge System.The conservation story is also tied to wildlife art. The first Federal Duck Stamp Contest was held in 1949, when 65 artists submitted 88 designs. The Federal Register notes that it remains the only art competition of its kind sponsored by the US government.Today, the US FWS holds the annual competition, with the winning artwork becoming the design for the following year's stamp. The contest gives the programme a changing visual identity while keeping wildlife at its centre.The designs have also evolved alongside the programme. The Federal Register records changes intended to reinforce the connection between the stamp, waterfowl hunting heritage and conservation. Artists are required to work within rules governing eligible waterfowl and the overall theme.The scale of the programme has changed considerably since that first $1 stamp. BirdNote recorded that by 2014, Duck Stamp sales had raised about $900 million and helped save or create 5.5 million acres of wetland, riparian and grassland habitat.
Article Summary: In 1934, the United States introduced a small annual stamp that linked waterfowl hunting directly to wetland conservation. The first one cost $1 and featured mallards, with artwork created by conservationist and cartoonist J.N. Ding Darling. More than nine decades later, the Federal Duck Stamp has raised over $1.3 billion and helped conserve over 6 million acres of habitat.

Article Title: Body of 10-year-old boy missing from Delhi found in nearby forest area
Article Text:
Cops and forensic team can be seen. (AI image)

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: The body of a 10-year-old boy who had gone missing from his home in Delhi's Bawana area was found in a forested area near a cemetery, with injury marks on his hands and legs, police said Tuesday.The boy, identified as Intzar, was reported missing on Sunday after he was last seen playing in a lane near his home in Bawana, police said.Around 3 pm on Monday, police received a PCR call about the body of a child lying in a blood-soaked condition in the Narela Industrial Area. A police team reached the spot and recovered the body.The body was sent for post-mortem examination and police are awaiting the report to ascertain the cause of death, an official said.Crime and forensic teams were also called to the spot and evidence was collected, police said.According to Intzar's father, Ayub, the boy was playing near their house around 11.30 am on Sunday when he suddenly went missing.The family searched the surrounding areas and asked several people about his whereabouts. When they could not trace him, a missing person report was lodged with the police.The family had also shared Intzar's photograph with a person who operates a swing in the area.On Monday afternoon, the man informed them that the body of a child had been found in the nearby forest area after shepherds spotted it.When the family reached the spot, they identified the body as that of Intzar, his father said.Ayub said the injury marks on the child's body raised suspicion that he may have been murdered. He also said the family had no enmity with anyone and that Intzar had never gone towards the forested area, leaving it unclear how he reached there.Police said they are scanning CCTV footage from the area and questioning local residents and other persons.The exact cause and circumstances of the death will be clear after the post-mortem examination, police said.
Article Summary: The boy, identified as Intzar, was reported missing on Sunday after he was last seen playing in a lane near his home in Bawana. Police received a PCR call about the body of a child lying in a blood-soaked condition in the Narela Industrial Area.

Article Title: Why should thousands suffer for one VIP?
Article Text:
Recent visits by foreign dignitaries to Rajghat have led to significant traffic disruptions for Delhi commuters ( AI image)

Rajghat visit: Protocol or tradition?

But it does not have to end in gridlock

What commuters faced

45+ MINUTES

25+ MINUTES

Advisory came. But when?

It is not a sudden visit. MEA told TOI in the past

Extent of ripple effect

What appeared to make the difference?

Big question

What traffic police said





For commuters, this has become a repeat ordeal every time a visiting head of state takes a trip to Rajghat. The latest movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin Monday once again left commuters stranded mid-journey with roads sealed and no viable alternate route for many. Some found themselves stuck in a traffic no-man’s land, waiting for restrictions to lift before they could resume their journeys. Others were forced to turn back or wait as vehicles piled up on key arteries. The visit may last minutes. The disruption can stretch for hours.A visit to Rajghat is not mandatory for visiting foreign leaders.But over the years, paying homage at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial has become an important part of the itinerary for visiting heads of state.MEA has said such visits have acquired significance as a mark of respect to Gandhi, with foreign leaders often considering it important to include Rajghat in their programmes.There are exceptions. Gulf leaders have generally avoided the visit for religious reasons. The Saudi king, who was chief guest for Republic Day in 2006, did not visit Rajghat, and the Saudi crown prince has also not done so during his recent visits.There was one notable recent exception: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s visit in Dec.The familiar pattern was expected: a VIP movement, restrictions and severe congestion around ITO.But the experience was different.There was congestion. It cleared within minutes. Traffic kept moving. The standstill did not stretch into hours.Stuck at ITOStuck at PWD HQComplaints on social media described chaos around ITO, with commuters questioning the lack of traffic regulation and on-ground monitoring.Delhi Traffic Police did issue an advisory for the Rajghat programme — at 9.09am, for a programme scheduled from 10am to noon.By that time the advisory came, many commuters were already on the road.Security restrictions may be triggered by a VIP movement, but the movement itself is not necessarily a last-minute event. An official aware of the security arrangements told TOI in the past that Delhi Police’s VIP security wing is informed well in advance about programmes involving visiting heads of state. In some cases, police may get information 10 days ahead.Under MHA guidelines, traffic stoppages for protected persons are meant to facilitate the movement of the President, Vice-President and Prime Minister, as well as visiting foreign dignitaries given President/PM-level security cover.Police can therefore have 7-10 days to prepare.A chief liaison officer (CLO) is also appointed by MHA to coordinate efforts among different agencies for the movement.Advance warning.Sustained deployment.Traffic kept moving.For thousands using ITO and surrounding corridors every day, the question is simple: If it can be managed better once, why does every VIP movement have to feel like a fresh traffic emergency?When roads are sealed without a workable alternative, commuters can be left with nowhere to go. Traffic backs up on adjoining roads, junctions choke and a short security restriction can turn into an hours-long commute. The Putin visit showed advance planning can work wonders.Sources from traffic said this was MEA protocol. “As far as advisories are concerned, we will see if it was not issued in advance this time, as it is part of the usual exercise now. Further, the traffic is stopped for the shortest time possible”
Article Summary: Recent visits by foreign dignitaries to Rajghat have led to significant traffic disruptions for Delhi commuters. Some found themselves stuck in a traffic no- man's land, waiting for restrictions to lift before they could resume their journeys. The latest movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin Monday once again left commuters stranded.

Article Title: MHT-CET 2027: Stakeholders for offline exam
Article Text:
Stakeholders including admissions counsellors and parents gathered in Azad Maidan to protest against the MHT-CET 2026 exam schedule.





MUMBAI: MHT-CET 2027 should be held offline, with each of its two attempts conducted for all candidates on a single day, and the first scheduled after students have had time to prepare, an admissions counsellor and a parents' representative urged.Yogeshwar Gutte, an admissions counsellor, and Narayan Shingare, who represented parents of students who took MHT-CET 2026, were among the 50-odd stakeholders who came from Latur, Ahmednagar, Nagpur and Pune to protest in Azad Maidan Monday. Later, they met state CET Cell commissioner Dilip Sardesai and said the exam schedule must account for Maharashtra State Board calendar. They called for the first attempt in the last week of Jan or in Feb, preferably after board exam, and for papers to follow state board syllabus. Their appeal follows concerns over the 2026 exam and the 2026- 27 engineering admission process. - Hemali Chhapia
Article Summary: Stakeholders including admissions counsellors and parents gathered in Azad Maidan to protest against the MHT-CET 2026 exam schedule. They called for the first attempt in the last week of Jan or in Feb, preferably after board exam, and for papers to follow state board syllabus.

Article Title: Banganga fish deaths: BMC plans 10 artificial ponds, more oxygenation pumps ahead of Pitru Paksha
Article Text:
BMC plans to create ten artificial ponds around Banganga tank to address fish death concerns.





MUMBAI: The BMC will set up 10 artificial ponds around Banganga tank at Walkeshwar and increase the number of oxygenation pumps at the site after a large number of fish were found dead in the water body, civic officials said on Monday.Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha inspected the tank following the fish deaths and reviewed measures being taken to protect the water body, particularly during Pitru Paksha, when thousands of people visit the site for pind daan and other religious rituals.D ward assistant municipal commissioner Santosh Salunkhe and local corporator Sunny Sanap were present during the inspection.Officials were asked to ensure that material used during religious rituals is not dumped into the tank or around its premises. Lodha appealed to citizens to opt for environment-friendly methods of performing pind daan and avoid putting oil, ghee, sweets and other offerings into the water.BMC officials were asked to step up cleaning and waste management during the remaining days of the period, which ends on Saturday, and continue the measures thereafter. Officials said some materials used in rituals can affect aquatic life.The civic administration had undertaken a cleanliness drive at the site as part of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan'.A resident, Sanjay Shirkhe, said, "The authorities were well aware that such a scenario would arise and hence should have taken steps in advance by barricading the tank before the fish deaths took place."
Article Summary: BMC plans to set up 10 artificial ponds around Banganga tank at Walkeshwar. A large number of fish were found dead in the water body. Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha inspected the tank following the fish deaths. Lodha appealed to citizens to opt for environment-friendly methods of performing pind daan.

Article Title: El Nino impact: 10% water cut in Maharashtra from Oct 16
Article Text:
The state govt GR says a special campaign should be launched to stop illegal water extraction from reservoirs, canals, rivers, lakes and other water sources





Mumbai: In view of the widespread drought and the El Nino factor likely to stretch into next year, water resources department has directed rural and urban local bodies including municipal corporations to impose a 10% cut on water consumption by October 16. The supply should be increased depending on water supply till August 31, 2027, it said.In a govt resolution issued on Monday, it also directed that 10% of the fresh water bodies of each major reservoir should be kept aside as an emergency reserve.“Drinking water will be the main priority. Water will be released for irrigation only after meeting drinking water, livestock and fodder requirements,” said water resources minister Girish Mahajan. The measures have been announced with a view to preserving available water till August 31, 2027.Industries have been asked to develop facilities to reuse or recycle 30% of their total water consumption.Treated waste-water should be used for public gardens, orchards, allotments and other green areas. Also, for construction, industrial processes, washing, green areas, gardens and other non-potable uses, the GR says.If any water remains surplus, then rabi season paddy cultivation should get priority. After that, other seasonal crops will be considered and lastly, perennial crops, the GR says.A special campaign should be launched to stop illegal water extraction from reservoirs, canals, rivers, lakes and other water sources. Joint teams of Revenue, Police, and Water Resources officials should organise regular inspections and patrols. Unauthorised vehicles, pipelines, pumps and other equipment should be seized and strict action should be taken.In reservoirs where the available fresh water reserves have been exhausted or are insufficient, the possibility of using the dead water reserves for fresh water should be examined. While using dead water reserves, the structural safety of the land, the technical feasibility of irrigation and other technical aspects should be considered, the GR says.For major projects whose scope of work is in more than one district, the water utilisation plan should be finalised by Canal Advisory Committee under the chairmanship of water resources minister.For other major, medium and small projects, the water utilisation plan should be finalised by Monitoring Committee under the chairmanship of guardian minister, it said.
Article Summary: Rural and urban local bodies including municipal corporations to impose a 10% cut on water consumption by October 16. The supply should be increased depending on water supply till August 31, 2027. 10% of fresh water bodies of each major reservoir should be kept aside as an emergency reserve.

Article Title: 2 charred to death, 12 hurt as firecrackers stocked in trader’s house in Hingoli explode
Article Text:
Police said repeated explosions made the firefighters’ task difficult

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

TOI





At least two people were charred to death and 12 others injured after a large quantity of firecrackers stored in a trader’s house in the densely populated Marwadi Galli area of Hingoli city caught fire on Monday evening, triggering a series of explosions that engulfed neighbouring houses and hampered rescue operations.District collector Rahul Gupta confirmed the deaths and said a municipal council employee was among those who suffered severe burn injuries. He said preliminary investigations indicated that the firecrackers had been stocked in the house ahead of Diwali.“Rescue operation is underway. Preliminary probe revealed that the firecrackers were stored illegally in a house ahead of the Diwali festival . Two deaths have so far been confirmed. One of them was a man working for the trader. Appropriate legal action will be initiated against the guilty after the rescue operation,” Gupta toldOfficials said they were yet to identify all the deceased and injured. An official said the blaze started around 7.30 pm after the stockpile of firecrackers inside the house caught fire. The resulting explosions rapidly intensified the blaze, which spread to at least two adjoining houses, causing extensive damage.Multiple fire brigade vehicles were rushed to the spot as emergency teams battled the flames. During the operation, one fire brigade vehicle caught fire, adding to the rescuers’ difficulties.The injured were shifted to Govt Medical College and Hospital in Hingoli, while the bodies of the deceased were also taken there for post-mortem procedures.A senior police officer said the large quantity of stored firecrackers posed a major challenge for rescue and firefighting teams. Repeated explosions prevented firefighters from approaching the affected structures, delaying efforts to bring the blaze under control.The incident triggered panic in the narrow lanes of Marwadi Galli, with thick plumes of smoke and continuous explosions sending residents fleeing the area. Authorities evacuated people living in the immediate vicinity as firefighters worked to prevent the fire from spreading further in the crowded neighbourhood.Officials said the exact cause of the fire remained under investigation. The extent of damage to the affected houses and other nearby property is yet to be assessed. The incident raised questions about how such a large quantity of firecrackers was stored in a residential locality.
Article Summary: A large quantity of firecrackers stored in a trader’s house in the densely populated Marwadi Galli area of Hingoli city caught fire on Monday evening. Repeated explosions prevented firefighters from approaching the affected structures, delaying efforts to bring the blaze under control.

Article Title: Burglars steal 17 tola gold, 2kg silver from flat in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Three unidentified burglars allegedly broke into a locked flat at Sai Srushti Park on Paithan Road and stole around 17 tolas of gold jewellery and 2kg of silver items early on Oct 4, police said.The flat had been locked since Aug 21 as owner Sneha Borgaonkar, 45, and her husband were staying at their second house in Samtanagar. A neighbour alerted her around 12.30pm after finding the flat’s door open and household articles scattered.“After checking the apartment’s CCTV footage, we found three unidentified people entering the premises between 4.45am and 5.30am. We are examining the footage and other technical evidence to identify and trace the suspects,” Satara police station inspector Krishna Shinde said.The burglars allegedly broke open a cupboard locker and took the valuables, including jewellery that had been in the family for decades.Police have registered a case against three unidentified persons and launched a search for them.
Article Summary: Three unidentified burglars allegedly broke into a locked flat and stole around 17 tolas of gold jewellery and 2kg of silver items. The flat had been locked since Aug 21 as owner Sneha Borgaonkar, 45, and her husband were staying at their second house in Samtanagar.

Article Title: ​Upto Rs 25k fine, criminal case for water wastage in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Amol Yedge, municipal commissioner

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Residents of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city wasting water or not fixing leakages will face a fine of Rs5,000 for first offence, Rs10,000 for second and Rs25,000 plus criminal offence for third time after Oct 15.Municipal commissioner Amol Yedage has set the Oct 15 deadline for completing all repair works related to household connections, leaking taps and internal pipelines in the wake of drought situation. After that, if leakage or wastage is found, penal action will be taken.“Water conservation is a collective responsibility of all. Residents should use available water sparingly and cooperate with the municipal water supply system. Do not waste water in any form,” Yedage said.The civic administration has warned that washing vehicles on roads, washing roads outside houses or wasting water in any other manner during the drought will attract fines and criminal cases.“Residents should close taps immediately after filling, ensure water does not flow on roads and drains, and fit proper taps to all connections,” Yedge said.The civic body also appealed not to use electric motors or pumps to directly draw water from municipal pipelines in areas where supply is adequate.It has also appealed that unauthorised tap connections should be regularized immediately and no tampering of pipelines without permission should be done.While residents at large have welcomed the appeal for water conservation, many said the civic body should also pay heed to leakage in the main water pipeline and other distribution works. “The old main water pipeline drawing water from Jayakwadi dam upto a pumping station at Farola itself has many leakages, causing wastage of water. Similarly, internal distribution networks are also porus at many places,” Suhas Patil, a resident, said.
Article Summary: Residents of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city wasting water will face a fine of Rs5,000 for first offence. The civic administration has warned that washing vehicles on roads, washing roads outside houses or wasting water in any other manner will attract fines and criminal cases.

Article Title: Nanded dist administration disconnects 51 power points in crackdown on illegal water lifting
Article Text:
Action against motors drawing water illegally from backwaters of Vishnupuri dam in Nanded

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Push for fodder literacy campaign





Nanded district administration, in a massive action against illegal water lifting, has disconnected electricity to 51 Distribution Points (DPs) of MSEDCL and also removed 215 motors drawing water from the Godavari river and Vishnupuri reservoir.District collector Rahul Kardile said the drive is aimed to protect drinking water stock for Nanded city and villages situated along the Godavari riverbank in view of the prevailing drought situation.“Unauthorized lifting has been a major cause for depletion of water storage that is earmarked for drinking purposes. By curbing the illegal use, we aim to conserve available water and ensure its judicious use for the coming months,” he said.Acting on instructions from Nanded tehsildar Sanjay Warkad, joint teams of the revenue department, MSEDCL and police conducted coordinated raids in Rahati, Jaitapur, Someshwar, Pimpalgaon Kor, Borgaon, Thugaon, Markad, Pimpalgaon Nimji, Kallal, Vishnupuri and Kotitirth.“During the crackdown, the teams snapped power connections of DPs that were used for illegally lifting water and dismantled motor pump sets installed without permission along the river and reservoir periphery,” Warkad said.Nanded city largely depends on Vishnupuri reservoir for its drinking water supply and administration fears shortage if illegal lifting continues unchecked. The district administration has made it clear that the drive against unauthorized water lifting will continue in coming days.“Strict penal action will be taken in future against elements indulging in water theft,” Warkad said.Nanded district administration has begun planting perennial Napier grass on nala bunds, silt-spread areas and wetlands as part of its fodder literacy campaign. At Sayal village in Loha taluka, Napier fodder was planted and livestock owners attended demonstrations on enriching poor-quality dry fodder and preparing mur-ghas, or silage.
Article Summary: Nanded district administration has disconnected electricity to 51 Distribution Points (DPs) of MSEDCL and removed 215 motors drawing water from the Godavari river and Vishnupuri reservoir. District collector Rahul Kardile said the drive is aimed to protect drinking water stock for Nanded city.
